Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

journalist noun

also journalists, newspaperman, newspaper reporter, reporter, reporters, news reporter, journalism, the press, press conference

modern

Traupman 167, 335, 370
M-O s.v. journalist (Egger)

diurnārius, diurnāriī m.

noun, second declension

a journalist

From diurna, the daily record (ācta diurna). Lewis & Short has the word once, late, for a keeper of a day-book (Cod. Theod. 8.4.8). A woman is diurnāria (Traupman). Traupman gives the same word for a reporter.

Other words

  • relātor, relātōris m. — a reporter

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. reporter (Egger)

    Classically the mover of a motion in the senate (Balbus in Cic. Att. 8.15a.2), late a narrator; an inscription names a recorder of auctions (Lewis & Short).

  • diurnāria ars — journalism

    also used · modern · Traupman 167; Traupman 335
